stepBody:
After this background study, the team goes on to explore the relationship between consumption of sugary drinks and blood sugar level. When the team collected the data on $$	ext{drink\_soda},$$ it also collected the following data on the same individuals.
• $$	ext{blood\_sugar}:$$ The pre-breakfast blood sugar level measured by the research team in the unit of millimoles per liter. (type: np.float)
• $$	ext{t2d}:$$ An indicator of whether the individual has type $$2$$ diabetes, where a value of $$1$$ indicates type $$2$$ diabetes, and $$0$$ indicates no type $$2$$ diabetes. (type: int)
To study the relationship, the team fit the following linear regression model over the data
$$\hat{y}=	heta_0+	heta_1 x_1+	heta_2 x_2$$
where $$y$$ is blood sugar, $$x_1$$ is drink soda and $$x_2$$ is t2d.
Suppose the optimal estimated parameters are $$\hat{	heta}_0=5.1$$ and $$\hat{	heta}_1=2.8$$ and $$\hat{	heta}_2=3.8$$
What is the interpretation of $$\hat{	heta}_2?$$ Explain in one sentence.
answerLatex: $$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the predicted increase in blood sugar for someone who has type $$2$$ diabetes relative to someone who does not have type $$2$$ diabetes, holding soda drinking status constant.
choices: $$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the predicted increase in blood sugar for someone who has type $$2$$ diabetes relative to someone who does not have type $$2$$ diabetes, holding soda drinking status constant.
$$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the predicted increase in blood sugar for someone who drinks soda relative to someone who does not drink soda, holding type $$2$$ diabetes status constant.
$$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the predicted blood sugar for someone who has type $$2$$ diabetes and drinks soda.
$$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the predicted probability that an individual has type $$2$$ diabetes given their blood sugar level.
$$\hat{\theta}_2$$ is the average blood sugar level among the surveyed adults who have type $$2$$ diabetes.
